turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period of at least four days when you felt unusually irritable or upbeat and had much more energy than usual?
turns.patient_response:
Four days of being upbeat or irritable? Um, no, I... I don't think I've ever tracked a four-day stretch like that. Energy is a weird thing, anyway. Energy can't be created or destroyed, right? That's the first law of thermodynamics. It just changes forms. Like kinetic energy turning into thermal energy when you hit the brakes on a car. The brake pads clamp down on the rotors, and the friction generates a massive amount of heat. That's why high-performance sports cars use carbon-ceramic brakes instead of steel. They can handle the extreme temperatures without warping. Carbon is so versatile. I mean, we were talking about diamonds earlier, but it's also in graphite, which is what pencil lead is made of. It's crazy that the same element can be the hardest substance on earth and also soft enough to write on paper just because of how the atoms are arranged. Atoms are mostly empty space, which is hard to wrap your head around. If you took all the empty space out of the atoms of every human on earth, the entire human race would fit into the volume of a sugar cube. 

But no, to answer your question, I haven't really noticed any four-day periods of having way too much energy or being super irritable. I just don't have an answer for that.
